SPECIAL EDITION · TECH TALK

Take off the old t-shirt.
Think new.

The power of AI in an engineer's hands — a story about how technology helps you break the boundaries of expertise, even when you think “I can't do this”.

● CONTEXT

An engineer who doesn't understand engines

Technical education? ✓. Combustion engines? ✗. Garden machinery and cars were never my domain.

Spring garden prep at my parents’ place. A Szentkirály Kertgépek rotavator won’t start after winter. Service shops are fully booked. Mom wants it done right now.

● LESSON #1

AI as an advisor, but not an infallible god

01
I asked AI
Checklist: oil, spark plug, filters, carburetor.
02
I bought the kit
AI “confirmed” the engine name. It didn’t fit.
!
Generation mismatch
AI couldn’t see the label. I didn’t verify it.
#1

AI is a powerful helper, but humans must validate the results

Without critical thinking and verifying details, AI can lead you down a dead end.

● LESSON #2

Understanding the connections — Weekend expert

Precise inputs
I gave AI the exact data from the manufacturing label.
Step-by-step guidance
AI guided me through each step. Not just to fix it, but to understand it.
Result
The rotavator started. Garden done. New skill acquired.
#2

With the right inputs, AI becomes the best teacher

For the first time, I understood how the machine works — not just “fix it”, but truly comprehend it.

● SYMBOLISM

Old t-shirt. New mindset.

During the repair, I was wearing an old, worn-out Telekom t-shirt that’s 20 years old.

“I don’t know how to do this.”
“This is not my job.”

We cling to old identities and limits — just like we cling to old t-shirts that no longer hold together.

👕 ➡ 🧠

Take off the old t-shirt. With AI, nothing is impossible.

The barriers between disciplines are fading.

● FOR WORK
🌍
Outside the comfort zone
Every day we face tasks outside our expertise.
⚡
“Expert at everything”
AI lets us become experts in record time.
🚀
Courage changes the rules
The right tool in the hands of a brave person.

Don’t be afraid of things that seem impossible.

Thank you for reading.

 

That's it - a borrowed one, but a good one. Go fix something outside your job description this summer, badly-fitting parts and all.

See you in September.

Tomas
